newsitem.title: USA: Most states say revenues on track - report.
newsitem.headline: Most states say revenues on track - report.

text.p: Most states expect revenue collections will exceed or meet estimates for the remainder of their fiscal years, according to a report from the National Conference of State Legislatures.

The group's State Fiscal Outlook for 1997 showed 29 states expecting revenues to exceed initial estimates, 19 states and the District of Columbia expecting to meet estimates, with only Hawaii and Idaho projecting a "slight decline" in revenues.
"Overall, states report that they are in good fiscal shape as the new year begins and work begins on (fiscal) 1998 state budgets," the report said.

For fiscal 1998, 17 states said tax cuts are likely to be considered during their 1997 legislative sessions, according to the report. Meanwhile, six states are eyeing an increase in their gasoline excise taxes that would be tied to major highway infrastructure improvements.

Other issues on state legislative agendas include implementing welfare reform, funding primary and secondary education, funding corrections and addressing Medicaid funding requirements, the report said.
